THE COMMENCEMENT OF SALVATION IS THE HOLY SPIRIT’S WORK.
There are many means of grace, and let us speak as highly of them as ever we can; we would be far from depreciating them; they are of the highest value;
But my brethren, no man was ever saved by the means of grace apart from the Holy Spirit.
there is no life for the soul apart from the breath of the Divine Spirit.
when the fountain-head floweth with water then they are full,
then these are wells without water, clouds without rain;
Nor is the salvation of any sinner commenced in him by a minister or by a priest
he seized the censer and would burn incense as a priest before the Lord God;
that can begin the work with us—no, not in the use of the ceremony.
And, my brethren, it is quite certain that no man ever begins the new birth himself.
Well the dead may be made alive, but the dead cannot make themselves alive, for the dead can do nothing.
Besides, it is a creation; we are created anew in Christ Jesus.
a true desire after true salvation by the true Spirit, is a certain index that the salvation already is there in the germ and in the bud
Be certain, therefore, that God the Holy Spirit must begin, since none else can do so.

You shall not know which cometh first; they are, very likely, begotten in us at the same moment.
We must always learn to distinguish between regeneration and conversion.
Conversion is a thing which is caused by regeneration, but regeneration is the very first act of God the Spirit in the soul.
It is true that one of the earliest developments of life is conviction of sin;
The sinner knows nothing about how it is done, nor do any of us understand it. “Thou understandest not the wind—it bloweth where it listeth;” but we see its effects.
they were no longer dead in sin, no longer without thought, without hope, without spiritual capacity, but they had begun to live.

The man begins to feel that he is a sinner; why did he not feel that before?
He begins to feel the exceeding weight and evil of transgression; his heart trembles, his very flesh quivers
the new life discovers the sin and evil of the past condition of the man
the next thing the Holy Spirit doth is, to teach the soul that it is utterly incapable of saving itself.
